import pandas as pd

# Read the raw Eurostat data
df = pd.read_csv("outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv")

# Pivot the data: rows are city_id + year, columns are indicator_id, values are the measure
# First, ensure we have the right columns
print("Columns in raw data:", df.columns.tolist())

# Pivot: index on city_id and year, columns on indicator_id, values on the value column
# The value column is typically named 'value' or similar
value_col = [c for c in df.columns if c.lower() in ['value', 'measure', 'amount', 'amount_value']]
if not value_col:
    # Try to find numeric column that isn't id or year
    numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include='number').columns.tolist()
    id_like_cols = [c for c in df.columns if 'id' in c.lower() or 'name' in c.lower() or 'year' in c.lower() or 'indicator' in c.lower()]
    value_col = [c for c in numeric_cols if c not in id_like_cols]
    
if value_col:
    value_col = value_col[0]
else:
    raise ValueError("Cannot determine value column")

print("Value column:", value_col)

# Pivot the table
pivoted = df.pivot_table(
    index=['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'],
    columns='indicator_id',
    values=value_col,
    aggfunc='first'  # Use first in case of duplicates
)

# Flatten multi-level column index
pivoted.columns = pivoted.columns.droplevel(0) if hasattr(pivoted.columns, 'droplevel') else pivoted.columns

# Reset index to make city_id, city_name, year regular columns
pivoted = pivoted.reset_index()

# Sort for consistency
pivoted = pivoted.sort_values(['city_id', 'year']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Save the output
pivoted.to_csv("outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv", index=False)
print("Output saved to outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv")
print("Shape:", pivoted.shape)
print("Columns:", pivoted.columns.tolist())
</solution_file>
